title: Surface billed_tokens + cache_hit fields in Usage API client
author: Monica Patel
release_notes: Python SDK: Usage API now exposes billed token counts and cache hit attribution (when available) to match invoice/usage exports. No breaking changes; new fields are optional and default to None when not returned by the API.
body: Context: As part of the metering hardening workstream, the Usage API is being extended to include fields that distinguish billed vs raw tokens, and to attribute cache hits where applicable. Finance/RevOps and customers have asked for a consistent way to reconcile invoice line items with usage exports, particularly around retries/fallback, caching, and token counting semantics. This PR updates the Python SDK usage client and response models to surface these new fields so customers can self-serve reconciliation and internal analytics. What changed: (1) Added optional response fields to usage records: billed_prompt_tokens, billed_completion_tokens, billed_total_tokens, and cache_hit (bool) + cache_hit_tokens (int, optional). (2) Updated the usage client to pass through the fields without forcing schema validation failures on older servers (gracefully handles missing fields). (3) Added docstrings + README snippet describing the difference between raw tokens and billed tokens, including how to treat None values during rollout. (4) Added unit tests using recorded fixtures for both pre-field and post-field payloads. (5) Added a short migration note for customers parsing usage exports into typed dataclasses/Pydantic models. Notes/semantics: billed_* fields are what Redwood uses for pricing and invoicing for Hosted API. raw token fields (prompt_tokens/completion_tokens/total_tokens) remain the underlying model tokenization counts, but may not reflect billing adjustments due to caching and platform behavior. cache_hit indicates the request was served partially or fully from cache; when present, cache_hit_tokens represents the tokens not executed on GPU (for attribution/analytics) and should not be assumed equal to a discount unless contractually specified. Rollout: Backend is shipping fields behind a gradual rollout; SDK must tolerate missing fields. This PR intentionally does not rename existing fields to avoid breaking changes. Related: redwood/pr-27485 (Expose cache-hit and billed token fields in usage API).
commits: sdk(usage): add billed_* token fields and cache hit attribution to UsageRecord
sdk(usage): make response parsing tolerant to missing optional fields
tests(usage): add fixtures for pre/post metering-field rollout payloads
docs: add migration note and examples for billed vs raw tokens
conversation: Nadia Rahman (review): Can we confirm naming matches the API fields exactly? We should avoid the SDK inventing its own names unless we document mapping. Also, for cache attribution: should cache_hit_tokens be optional even when cache_hit=true? Monica Patel (author): Yep — aligned with the backend response naming (snake_case). cache_hit_tokens stays Optional[int]; during rollout the backend can emit cache_hit without tokens for some models/regions until backfill completes. Added docstring + tests to cover cache_hit=true, cache_hit_tokens=None. Chris Osei (review): Please add a small migration note for customers who deserialize usage records into strict schemas; this will help CS/Sales when customers compare invoice vs usage exports. Monica Patel (author): Added a section to docs/usage.md and a snippet in README: 'If you use strict parsing, allow unknown fields or update your schema to include the optional billed_* fields.' Allison Grant (review): I’d prefer a single billed_tokens field but I understand backend is splitting by prompt/completion. Can we also include billed_total_tokens for convenience? Monica Patel (author): Added billed_total_tokens to the model and wired it through. Also updated the example to compute totals defensively if the server only returns prompt/completion in early rollout. Nadia Rahman (follow-up): Tests look good. One more thing: ensure we don’t treat missing billed_* as 0; None is important for rollout. Monica Patel (author): Updated parsing defaults to None; tests assert None when absent. Approvals: Nadia Rahman approved. Chris Osei approved. Allison Grant approved.
notes: Customer-facing behavior: No functional change unless the server returns new fields; fields will appear in SDK responses automatically. Internal: This is a dependency for Sales Enablement guidance around billed vs raw tokens and cache attribution during meter hardening.
